raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Fix https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59065

With DCP > 1 and speculative decoding, FlashInfer MLA decode crashes when the decode batch is ragged, i.e. requests carry different numbers of query tokens. That happens whenever a request has fewer drafts than the others, and also during warmup. For example, Kimi-K3 with `-tp 2 -dcp 2` and DSpark fails at engine startup:

```
ValueError: causal_seqlens_kv_global must have shape (9,), got (2,)
```

Here a 1+7 request and a 1-token request make 9 decode tokens.

DCP cannot take the compact ragged path (`cum_seq_lens_q`), because it needs LSE. So ragged batches fall to the "uneven length" branch. That branch has two problems:

- **Shape mismatch.** It splits `q` into one row per token, but it keeps `block_table`, `seq_lens` and `causal_seqlens_kv_global` per request. FlashInfer then rejects the call.
- **Silent wrong reshape.** The branch is only taken when `num_decode_tokens % num_decodes != 0`. A ragged batch whose token count happens to divide evenly (e.g. 8 + 2 tokens) is instead `view`ed as a uniform 5 + 5 batch, and each request's rows attend to the wrong KV.

## Fix

A batch is now treated as ragged when `num_decode_tokens != num_decodes * max_query_len`. Ragged causal batches are split into single-token rows:

- `block_table` and `seq_lens` are expanded per row with the existing `_flattened_decode_metadata`.
- Each row's DCP bound is `T - (tokens of its request after it)`. FlashInfer defines `causal_seqlens_kv_global` as the global exclusive causal bound of each row's newest query token, and `dcp_tot_seq_lens` (`T`) already includes all of the request's query tokens.

The non-DCP causal path is unchanged; it already goes through `cum_seq_lens_q`.

## Not a duplicate

No open PR touches this branch. #56784 edits the same file, but only for backend selection.

## Test Plan

- Kernel check on GB200, run directly against `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla` with the cute-dsl backend, `cp_world=2`, both ranks, and `(T, q_len)` in `{(301, 8), (97, 8), (130, 4), (64, 1)}`:
  - One request with `q_len` rows and bound `T` gives bit-identical output and LSE (max error `0.0`) to `q_len` single-token rows bounded at `T - (q_len - 1 - j)`.
  - Negative control: bounding every split row at `T` gives a max output error of `0.26`.
- `tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_dcp.py`: `test_flashinfer_mla_forward_uses_native_dcp_api` is extended with a ragged `(3, 1)` batch. The new `ragged-causal` case fails without this change and passes with it.

```
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_dcp.py tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_decode.py
```

## Test Result

- `tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_dcp.py` + `tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_decode.py`: 23 passed, 1 skipped (GB200).
- Without the source change, only `ragged-causal` fails.
- An end-to-end run with Kimi-K3 was not done here. The `dcp2-*-dspark` cases in #59229 are strict xfails for this bug and will flip once this lands.

No output changes for batches that worked before, so no model eval was run.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

nodes.body:
Thanks for the fix! We validated the `flashinfer_mla.py` change at `1a6def812d94` with a controlled A/B run and confirmed that it resolves the startup crash reported in #59065 for our configuration.

Both runs used the same image, model, server flags and environment variables; the only runtime change was this PR’s patch to `flashinfer_mla.py`.

- **Hardware/configuration:** 2 nodes × 4 NVIDIA GB300, Ray executor, Kimi-K3 with TP=8, DCP=8, FlashInfer MLA, FP8 KV cache, and DSpark with 7 speculative tokens using the V2 model runner.
- **Base image:** `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-ac68c3087215e0a4f3cdfa218508c6aada57235d`
- **Software:** vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev396+gac68c3087`, FlashInfer `0.7.0.post1`, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`.

**Results:**

| | Unpatched | With this patch |
|---|---|---|
| Startup | Fails during `warmup_kernels` with `causal_seqlens_kv_global must have shape (9,), got (2,)` | Completes successfully |
| Serving | Never reached | 5/5 requests completed, 0 errors |

The serving check used synthetic prompts with 1,000 input / 1,000 requested output tokens, concurrency 1 and `ignore_eos=true`.

This validates startup and basic serving for the reported configuration. There was one run per arm, and no accuracy evaluation was performed. Multi-request ragged batches were exercised during warmup; we did not separately target the evenly divisible ragged case described in this PR.

*Drafted with assistance from Codex (GPT-6).*

✅ Triggered [Buildkite CI #94737](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94737) for commit `8412d35a8081`.

ℹ️ This PR is 815 commits behind upstream `main`. Merged upstream `main` into this branch as `8412d35a8081` before starting CI. Pull the branch before pushing more changes.

-def test_flashinfer_mla_forward_uses_native_dcp_api(monkeypatch, causal):

+def test_flashinfer_mla_forward_uses_native_dcp_api(monkeypatch, causal, query_lens):

@@ -106,8 +107,11 @@ def test_flashinfer_mla_forward_uses_native_dcp_api(monkeypatch, causal):

     )

+    lens = torch.tensor(query_lens)
     block_table = torch.tensor([[10], [20]], dtype=torch.int32)
     seq_lens = torch.tensor([4, 5], dtype=torch.int32)

     kernel = MagicMock(
         return_value=(
             torch.ones(
@@ -155,15 +159,17 @@ def test_flashinfer_mla_forward_uses_native_dcp_api(monkeypatch, causal):
 
     call = kernel.call_args.kwargs
     assert call["query"].shape == (kernel_batch, kernel_query_len, 24, 576)
-    expected_block_table = (
-        block_table if causal else block_table.repeat_interleave(query_len, dim=0)
-    )
-    expected_seq_lens = seq_lens if causal else seq_lens.repeat_interleave(query_len)
-    expected_global_seq_lens = (
-        global_causal_seq_lens
-        if causal
-        else global_causal_seq_lens.repeat_interleave(query_len)

+    expected_block_table = block_table

@@ -341,6 +341,8 @@ def forward_mqa(
         cum_seq_lens_q: torch.Tensor | None = None
         max_q_len: int | None = None
         row_req: torch.Tensor | None = None
+        # Per split row: query tokens of its request after it.
+        causal_rows_after: torch.Tensor | None = None
 
         if not attn_metadata.causal:
             # FlashInfer decode has no causal flag. Flatten each non-causal
@@ -357,15 +359,23 @@ def forward_mqa(
             # do not return on the ragged path (flashinfer #3238).
             cum_seq_lens_q = attn_metadata.decode.query_start_loc
